Requirements for a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) Degree in Public Health
In addition to College-wide requirements including Liberal Education Curriculum, students who plan to pursue a degree in
Public Health must take a minimum of 11 courses to fulfill degree requirements. The basic requirements for the degree are:
One semester of Biological Sciences: 3 Credits
BS 2100 - Biology for Non-science Majors Credits: 4
BS 2300 - Anatomy and Physiology I Lecture Credits: 3
OR
OR
BS 2310 - Anatomy and Physiology II Lecture Credits: 3
Eight core courses in Public Health: 32 Credits
* Prerequisite: MA 2000 or equivalent
** Prerequisite: PH 2000 and PH 3600, Pre or co-requisite: 4800
*** Prerequisite: PH 5900, senior status
PH 2000 - Introduction to Public Health Credits: 4
PH 3600 - Introduction to the Social Determinants of Health Credits: 4
PH 3610 - Introduction to the U.S. Health Care System Credits: 4
PH 4670 - Biostatistics Credits: 4 *
PH 4800 - Epidemiology Credits: 4
PH 4900 - Applied Practice Experience Credits: 4
PH 5900 - Senior Research Seminar I Credits: 4 **
PH 5920 - Senior Research Seminar II Credits: 4 ***
Three Public Health Department Electives: 12 Credits

Public Health Applied Practice Experience
All Public Health students must complete a 90-hour applied practice experience (e.g., internship). Depending on their inter‐
ests, students work in a wide variety of health settings. The experience is an integral part of the Public Health program.
